Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — encryption evidence request

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking SIG last week — we have one final set of follow-ups from our security team focused specifically on encryption/key custody. To complete our vendor risk review we need: 

- Short technical writeup of in-transit protections (TLS versions, mutual auth, cipher suites)
- At-rest encryption: algorithm, envelope encryption design (DEK/KEK), key storage location, and how keys are protected
- KMS/HSM topology: which KMS providers are used (hosted/cloud, customer-managed options), HSM vendor(s) and tamper-evidence controls
- Key rotation policy & evidence: rotation schedules for KEKs and DEKs, rotation automation, and recent rotation logs for the last 6 months
- Key custody & separation of duties: who can request rotation/unwrap, whether ops/devs have access, and how we log and audit those operations

Can you share the technical summary and attach supporting artifacts (rotation logs, HSM audit summary, architecture diagram) by EOD Oct 16? If you prefer a 30-minute call to walk through, we can schedule early next week.

Best,
Jillian

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 14:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up — encryption evidence request

Lauren / Rishi — draft below and attached artifacts. I included filenames in the manifest. Ask if you want changes; some items are redacted in the HSM summary per vendor agreement.

--- Technical summary (candidate for external delivery) ---
1) In-transit protections- All public endpoints use TLS 1.3 (minimum). We enforce strong cipher suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384) and forward secrecy.- Internal service-to-service traffic uses mutual TLS (mTLS) with short-lived client certificates (rotated daily via our internal CA).- Control-plane endpoints require mTLS + token-based auth; audit logs capture handshake details for correlation.

2) At-rest encryption and envelope design- Primary design: envelope encryption. Each data object is encrypted with a data encryption key (DEK) using AES-256-GCM. DEKs are wrapped by a key-encryption key (KEK) managed by our KMS.- DEK lifecycle: DEKs are generated per-object or per-batch depending on workload; defaults are weekly DEK rotation for persistent stores and per-session DEKs for ephemeral caches.- KEK lifecycle: customer root KEKs are hosted in a tenant-scoped CMK (cloud KMS) or customer-managed HSM depending on deployment. KEKs are rotated on a 12-month cycle by default; automated staggered rollouts avoid replay failures. Emergency rekey and forced rotation can be performed within 24 hours and is logged.

3) KMS / HSM topology- Hosted (Redwood cloud): primary KEKs are managed in AWS KMS (multi-account key policies) with AWS CloudHSM backing for high-assurance key material for select tenants.- Dedicated & Private deployments: we support customer-managed HSM (Thales Luna v6 / SafeNet) or on-prem CloudHSM clusters; in private mode the customer controls root key import and rotation if requested (BYOK).- HSM protections: tamper-evident hardware, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certification (vendor provided). HSM admin access is restricted to our crypto ops team; split knowledge enforced for key ceremony tasks.

4) Custody, access controls & separation of duties- Role separation: developers never have access to unwrapped KEKs. Crypto Ops can perform key lifecycle operations; requests require approval via the change control Jira workflow (JIRA-SEC-xxxx).- Access to KMS management ops is RBAC-controlled, requires MFA and admin justification. All key material access and unwrap operations are logged in audit trails (CloudTrail + internal audit collector).

5) Rotation evidence and logs included- kms-rotation-log-2028-Q3.csv (recent KEK rotation events, timestamps, requestor IDs)- hsm-audit-summary-2028-09.pdf (redacted HSM audit with vendor tamper logs)- dek-rotation-sample-2028-07.csv (sample DEK generation/rotation events)- encryption-architecture-diagram-v2.png (diagram of envelope flow & KMS/HSM boundaries)

6) Notes / limitations- Some vendor HSM logs are redacted where they contain hardware serials. We have provided the vendor-signed audit summary instead.- For hosted multi-tenant customers, tenant isolation uses tenant-scoped CMKs; we can provide additional attestations for single-tenant Dedicated deployments upon request.

--- end draft ---

I attached the files mentioned above. I included the CloudTrail-derived rotation log (kms-rotation-log-2028-Q3.csv) and a small sample of DEK rotation entries for reviewers to validate periodicity.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Platform Security

Custody & approvals (external-ready paragraph):

Quick summary highlights:
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 enforced; mTLS for internal and control plane; strong ciphers and forward secrecy.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM with envelope encryption (per-object DEKs wrapped by KEKs).
- Keys: KEKs managed in KMS with HSM-backed protections for high-assurance tenants; customer BYOK supported for private deployments.
- Rotation: DEKs rotated per workload (defaults weekly or per-session); KEKs rotated annually by default; emergency rotation within 24 hours.
- Custody & audit: separation of duties via Crypto Ops + change-control workflow; all unwrap/rotation ops logged in immutable audit.

If you'd like a short walkthrough, I'm available Tue/Wed morning next week — happy to schedule a 30-minute call with Neha and Rishi to walk through the artifacts.
